Honest caveat: it is a param path, so the probe never called it (it is in probe/paths-param.txt, absent from sweep.jsonl) and no live status was observed; the SPA also wraps it in no hook, so it has no rendering call site to copy field names from.
wrongly_excluded.correction: Add it as a new read, e.g. command_name "supply-chain run", description: "One daily shortage run in full by its id — the same detail as run-latest, for any run in the list, not just the newest." Expect the /supply-chain/runs/latest/ shape (run, rows, issues, verdict_progress, unassigned_red_rows), mark the shape UNPROBED, and render a 404 as 'no run with that id' the same way run-latest's NO_RUN 404 is rendered as an empty state.

wrongly_excluded.claim: Endpoint omitted from the study entirely (not published, no exclusion reason given).
wrongly_excluded.reason: It is a live, GET-only, read-only resolver and it is the shop-floor entry point for the whole module: scan the QR/barcode on a machine or spare and get the record back. SPA (maintenance.queries-C80VC0jM.js): `async lookupScan(e){return(await n.get(r.SCAN_LOOKUP,{params:{code:e}})).data}` — GET with a single `code` param; the hook is gated on `e.trim().length>0`. The sweep GET (no code) returned 404 with a business body in all three tenants: {"found":false,"code":"","detail":"No maintenance asset or spare matched this code."} — a get_or_create would have created a row and returned 200, so this one demonstrably does not write (confidence ~90%; residual doubt is that no hit-path body was captured). The write half of the scan flow is a different URL: POST /maintenance/scan/work-order/ (createWorkOrderFromScan), which returns 405 to GET and must never be generated.
wrongly_excluded.correction: Publish as a read: `maintenance scan-lookup --code <printed code>` — 'Scan lookup: find the asset or spare behind a QR/barcode printed on the shop floor.' Required param `code` (string, from the tag, not an id). Trap: a miss returns HTTP 404 with found:false and a plain detail line — that is 'no such tag', not a broken endpoint. Never generate anything for /maintenance/scan/work-order/ (POST-only, creates a work order).

wrongly_excluded.claim: Endpoint omitted from the study entirely (not published, no exclusion reason given).
wrongly_excluded.reason: Live GET, read-only stock lookup for one spare. Traps: one of --spare/--code is required (a bare call 404s); never send an empty string or 'ALL'; the spare master is empty in all three companies today so every lookup 404s — that is a data fact, and this is the local maintenance store, never SAP stock.

Carry the trap that the path's real verb is POST, so any method filter must key on the methods array, and the same page_size/timeout warning as the sessions list (JIVO_OIL returned HTTP 0 / RemoteDisconnected on both paths — a payload timeout, not a missing route).

refuted_claims.claim: Trap: 'gross_required = the quantity being produced x quantity_per_unit (3000 x 24 = 72000). quantity_per_unit is BOM consumption per unit made, NOT a pack or carton size.' And: 'Quantities are PIECES of the material (e.g. 269400 caps/bottles), not cartons and not tonnes.'
refuted_claims.reason: Two separate errors. (a) 'NOT a pack or carton size': for every per-bottle component observed, quantity_per_unit is numerically exactly the pack count, because the unit made is the case — 24.00000000 on both PM rows of the 24-PCS FG0000314, and 20.00000000 on all four GP-FG PM rows plus RM0000009. Telling a reader it is 'not a pack size' invites them to treat 24 as a genuine per-bottle consumption rate. (b) 'Quantities are PIECES of the material' is contradicted by the RM rows in the same payload: RM0000134 has on_hand 88.3000, committed 0.1600 and gross_required 11520 — fractional stock is not a piece count, and 11520 is litres (3000 cases x 3.84 L). The hedge that follows ('Don't convert without knowing the item's own UoM') is correct but is buried under a leading assertion that is wrong for every RM row. The formula itself is verified and stands: 72000-19228+51-0 = 52823, 72000-25464+121-0 = 46657, 11520-88.30+0.16 = 11431.86.
refuted_claims.correction: 'gross_required = units made x quantity_per_unit. quantity_per_unit is BOM consumption per UNIT MADE, and the unit made is a case — so for per-bottle components it comes out equal to the pack count (24 for a 24-PCS item, 20 for a 20-PCS one). The quantity's UoM is the MATERIAL's own UoM, not always pieces: PM rows are pieces (269400 caps/bottles) but RM rows can be litres or kg (RM0000134: on_hand 88.3, gross 11520 L). Fractional on_hand/committed is the tell. Resolve the code against SAP (OITM.InvntryUom) before converting.'

refuted_claims.claim: Trap: 'quantity is in PIECES (3000 bottles of a 24-PCS item), not cartons. Don't multiply by the pack count in the item name.'
refuted_claims.reason:
The row's own BOM arithmetic proves `quantity` counts CASES, not bottles. Sampled row (sweep.jsonl, /order-processing/production/): item FG0000314 'PET BOTTLE 160 MLS PUNJABI  JEERA 24 PCS', quantity 3000, with materials:
  * PM0000777 quantity_per_unit 24.00000000 -> gross_required 72000
  * PM0000584 quantity_per_unit 24.00000000 -> gross_required 72000
  * RM0000134 quantity_per_unit 3.84000000 -> gross_required 11520
3.84 / 24 = 0.16 exactly, i.e. 160 ml — so one 'unit made' contains 24 x 160 ml. If a unit were one bottle the liquid line would be 3000 x 0.16 = 480 L, not 11520 L; 11520 L is 3000 x 24 x 160 ml, the volume of 3000 cases. Two packing materials at exactly 24 per unit only make sense as 1-per-bottle x 24 bottles. The same pattern repeats independently on the GP-FG rows in /order-processing/materials/ (quantity_per_unit 20.00000000 on four PM codes AND on RM0000009, gross 269400 -> 13470 units made) — a 20-per-unit consumption of a raw material is only coherent if the unit is a 20-pack. Confidence high; what would settle it beyond doubt is RM0000134's UoM in SAP (OITM.InvntryUom), which was not read. Note this is the opposite of the ORDER-line convention, which the study got right (order line quantity 120, pack_size 12, cases 10 — genuinely pieces). Shipped as written, an operator multiplies 3000 by 24 and reports a 24x-inflated production plan.
refuted_claims.correction: 'quantity is the number of UNITS MADE, and the BOM shows that unit is the CASE/carton, not the bottle: 3000 units of a 24-PCS item = 3000 cases = 72,000 bottles = 11,520 L (the row's own RM line). Note this is the reverse of order lines, where quantity IS pieces. Multiply by the pack count to get bottles; do not treat 3000 as bottles.'

In GoodsReturnDetailPage-B7a3Dl9T.js the component computes `const c=t.basis==="INVOICE"` and renders: "Confirm the goods physically arrived" + (c ? " — this posts an A/R Returns document to SAP for the returned stock." : ". No SAP posting is done for non-invoice returns."). refuted_claims.claim: Trap: 'This is a plain detail route on its own primary key — it is NOT one of the get-or-create GET paths in this app (those take a foreign key and create a row on a miss). It is safe to read; do not confuse it with /quality-control/arrival-slips/{id}/inspection/.'
refuted_claims.reason: The first half is right; the cited counter-example is wrong. /quality-control/arrival-slips/{id}/inspection/ does not create a row on a miss. inspection.queries-CRAW2sOW.js wraps the GET specifically to handle a miss: 'async getForSlip(e){try{return(await a.get(i.QUALITY_CONTROL_V2.INSPECTION_FOR_SLIP(e))).data}catch(t){if(t.status===404)return null;throw t}}' — a get_or_create would never 404, so the 404 handler is proof the server returns one. Creation on that URL is a separate explicit POST ('async create(e,t){…await a.post(s,t)}'). The probe agrees: /quality-control/arrival-slips/1407/inspection/ returned 200 with a full inspection object (report_no, internal_lot_no, supplier_batch_lot_no, qa_chemist_approved_at and the rest) and 1329/inspection/ returned 404 'No MaterialArrivalSlip matches the given query'. Naming a safe endpoint as this app's canonical dangerous-GET example teaches the wrong lesson, and the real get-or-create risks in this registry go unnamed.
refuted_claims.correction: Fix the trap to cite the actual risky shapes in QUALITY_CONTROL_V2: ARRIVAL_SLIP_GET, which resolves to the same URL as ARRIVAL_SLIP_CREATE (/quality-control/po-items/{id}/arrival-slip/), and MATERIAL_TYPE_BY_SAP_ITEM (/quality-control/material-types/by-sap-item/{CODE}/), which takes a lookup key rather than a numeric id — both correctly left unpublished. Separately, /quality-control/arrival-slips/{id}/inspection/ is a safe GET-or-404 returning the full raw-material inspection record and is a reasonable candidate to publish as a new read (it is absent from shipped-command-names.json, so it would take a new name); if it is left out, leave it out for scope reasons, not on a false get-or-create claim.
